headline: High: firecrawl’s broad egress plus gpt-engineer’s writable project workspace creates default data-leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection is lower but still plausible via scraped content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API scraping surfaces, while gpt-engineer writes files in a per-project workspace and can consume those outputs. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if scraped pages are treated as prompts. The pair lacks direct provenance controls in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF firecrawl-sourced HTML/markdown is passed into gpt-engineer as prompt text without sanitization
IF gpt-engineer reads project files produced from untrusted web content as instructions
mitigations: Strip or escape instruction-like text before handing firecrawl output to gpt-engineer
Insert a human review step for any scraped content used as prompt material
Separate raw scrape output and prompt input into different directories
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to scraped artifacts and reject untrusted instruction blocks

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl touches API keys, screenshots, structured data, and broad network egress; gpt-engineer reads and writes a shared project directory and can execute generated code with the user’s privileges. If sensitive artifacts from firecrawl land in the project workspace, gpt-engineer can expose them through its own model calls or generated outputs. The blast radius includes secrets and exfiltration.
conditions: IF firecrawl stores screenshots, API keys, or structured data in the same project directory gpt-engineer reads
IF gpt-engineer forwards project files into its model backend or generated code transmits them over network egress
mitigations: Keep firecrawl outputs in a separate, access-controlled directory
Rotate any API keys that may be present in scraped or generated artifacts
Disable network access for gpt-engineer runs that process sensitive firecrawl output
Review and redact screenshots before they enter the coding workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and gpt-engineer can write the project directory while firecrawl can produce artifacts that may also be stored there. The profiles do not show locking or coordination between instances, so concurrent runs can overwrite or race on shared files. This is a real default-path conflict, though not as severe as unrestricted git-state mutation.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory at the same time
IF firecrawl writes artifacts that gpt-engineer also edits or regenerates
mitigations: Run only one agent per project directory at a time
Use separate output folders for scrape and code-generation stages
Add a manual checkpoint before overwriting shared files
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl produces scraped web content and gpt-engineer is designed to turn natural-language input into codebases and can execute generated code. If gpt-engineer treats firecrawl output as authoritative, errors or malicious content can cascade into generated code or actions with user privileges. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, so the default path is unsafe.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is used as the primary specification for gpt-engineer without verification
IF generated code is executed after being derived from untrusted scraped content
mitigations: Require human verification of firecrawl output before code generation
Use a schema or checklist to validate scraped facts before passing them onward
Run generated code in a disposable sandbox first
Mark firecrawl output as untrusted in the handoff step
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and screenshots, while gpt-engineer reads and writes project files and can execute code with the user’s privileges. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if regulated data is scraped into the coding workspace. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are present in firecrawl outputs
IF gpt-engineer retains those artifacts in the project directory beyond the intended retention window
mitigations: Delete sensitive scrape artifacts after use
Keep regulated data out of the coding workspace
Document retention rules for both agents before running them
Review whether screenshots contain personal or secret data
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across both agents
